title: Allow only licensed employees to do high-risk work
what: Not allow an employee to do high-risk work (such as crane or forklift operation, scaffolding, or dogging and rigging) unless the employee holds the right high-risk work licence.

sources.title: Occupational Health and Safety Regulations 2017 (Vic)
sources.publisher: Victorian Legislation (authorised version saved by the owner)
sources.locator: r 129 (S.R. No. 22/2017, authorised version 018, saved by the owner)
sources.quote: An employer must not allow an employee to perform high risk work unless the employee holds an appropriate high risk work licence in relation to the work.

administration.note: Issues the high-risk work licences and enforces the duty.

sources.title: Summary of the OHS Act 2004: General OHS Duties
sources.locator: Duties of employers to employees and contractors (section 21)
sources.quote: The OHS Act requires all employers to provide and maintain a working environment that is safe and without risks to health. This duty is to be met so far as is reasonably practicable.

triggers.note: When a worker is to do a class of high-risk work listed in the regulation's Schedule 3.

reach.condition: if its workers do high-risk work that needs a licence (such as operating cranes or forklifts, scaffolding, or dogging and rigging)
reach.note: Any business whose workers do licensed high-risk work, in any industry; most often construction, manufacturing, mining, transport and warehousing.

assessment.summary: A business must not let a worker do high-risk work (such as operating cranes or forklifts, scaffolding, or dogging and rigging) without seeing the worker's licence. Only licensed workers can be hired for that work.

marks.reason: Only licensed workers may do high-risk work, which narrows who can be hired for it.

assessment.confidence_note: Marked from the duty's design against the framework's guide; the safety benefit is not counted by the framework.
